name: Autohand Code

surfaces.label: Autohand Code CLI under Node (npm i -g autohand-cli, bins autohand, autohand-code, agent, ah), once running. The first statement of src/index.ts is process.title = 'Autohand Code', so on macOS (libuv overwrites the argv area, as the kimi row observed on this Mac with node 22) ps and KERN_PROCARGS2 show argv[0] = 'Autohand Code' and the original arguments are gone. Inferred from that analogy, never seen: Autohand is not installed here. Because the flags are gone, one title covers the interactive TUI, `-p` one-shots, `--mode rpc` and `--acp` (IDE and ADE clients), `--mode teammate` children and short subcommands; ps cannot tell them apart. Truncation risk: libuv cuts the title to the length of the original argv span, so a very short `node <path>` launch could show a prefix of 'Autohand Code'. The title has a space, so the probe's space-split ps fallback would miss it; the real KERN_PROCARGS2 argv is fine.

Autohand Code CLI under Node during the first moments, before the title is set (the ESM imports run first, so the original argv survives for the start-up window; inferred). Node's argv[1] is the path the shebang was run with, i.e. the bin symlink such as ~/.nvm/versions/node/<v>/bin/autohand or /opt/homebrew/bin/autohand, NOT .../autohand-cli/dist/index.js. `/bin/autohand` also matches `/bin/autohand-code`. The `ah` and `agent` bins are not matched: `agent` collides with Cursor's and Grok's, and `/bin/ah` would also be a prefix of `/bin/ahtraces`.

Autohand Code CLI as a compiled Bun binary (install.sh, Homebrew tap autohandai/code formula autohand-code, or the GitHub release tarball autohand-macos-arm64.tar.gz): one Mach-O `autohand` in ~/.local/bin (or /usr/local/bin as root, or the Homebrew bin) plus symlinks autohand-code, agent and ah. The kernel argv[0] is whatever name the shell was given: autohand, autohand-code, ah, or a full path. Whether Bun's process.title assignment retitles the process on macOS is NOT known; if it does, this process matches the first surface instead. Bare `agent` is deliberately not listed: the Autohand installers replace any existing `agent` on PATH (Cursor's, Grok's), and a bare `agent` argv[0] cannot be told from Grok Build's native `agent` by command line (same rule as the grok-build row). `ah` is a two-letter name, kept because it is a documented bin and an exact-basename match.

VS Code extension AutohandAI.vscode-autohand, Zed / JetBrains / JetBrains Air as custom ACP agents (`autohand --acp`), and any client that launches `autohand --mode rpc`. These start the same CLI as a child of the editor (Extension Host, Zed, the JetBrains IDE); the CLI child matches one of the tui surfaces above, so no separate process rule is given. The VS Code extension README on the Marketplace says release VSIX builds BUNDLE the CLI for macOS arm64 and x64 ('no separate CLI installation is required', falling back to `autohand` on PATH), so the editor's CLI child may run from the extension folder under a name and path not seen here (vsix not fetched); the tui surfaces match it only if its argv[0] basename is autohand, autohand-code, ah or autohand-macos-*, which is unverified.

Autohand Code Web (Continue in CLI / `autohand transfer <id>`) and the Autohand Code iOS app paired with `/go`. Nothing local to match; the iOS pairing runs a relay inside the CLI and turns on a `caffeinate` child (see working_signals).

session_store.note: The README promises only the directory (`Sessions are auto-saved to ~/.autohand/sessions/`). File names and shapes are from source (src/session/SessionManager.ts): sessions/<sessionId>/ holds conversation.jsonl (one SessionMessage per line: role, content, timestamp, toolCalls, name, tool_call_id, _meta; appended with fs.appendFile per message, so it is written when a message is committed, not per token), metadata.json (sessionId, createdAt, lastActiveAt, closedAt, projectPath, projectName, model, messageCount, summary, title, status active|completed|crashed, exitCode, type, usage, client, importedFrom, branch), state.json (workspace snapshot). sessions/index.json (+ index.json.lock) lists all sessions. sessionId is `<uuid-v4>-<Date.now() ms>`. AUTOHAND_HOME replaces ~/.autohand for everything here. `--ephemeral` runs write no session files. A quiet conversation.jsonl during a long model call or tool call is expected, so a stale mtime never proves idle.

pid_index.note: Not in the schema. THE way to map a live process to its session: a plain launch carries no session id in argv (`autohand resume <ref>` and `--fork <ref>` are positional or take a reference, not a --session-id flag), and the process retitles itself anyway. Source only (src/session/ActiveAgentRegistry.ts, src/core/agent.ts startActiveAgentHeartbeat), never seen live.
pid_index.file: <sessionId>.json, or <sessionId>.<instanceId>.json when peer communication is enabled. Directory mode 0700, file mode 0600, written atomically. Location moves to <sessions.communication.coordinationDirectory>/active-agents when that setting is set, and with AUTOHAND_HOME.
pid_index.keys: version, pid, sessionId, workspaceRoot, projectName, provider, model, mode (interactive|command|rpc in practice: the type also lists acp and teammate but resolveActiveAgentMode() only returns the first three), status (idle|working), startedAt, updatedAt, messageCount, contextPercent, tokensUsed, activity{phase (idle|thinking|editing|running_command|waiting_input), instruction, command, pathsWritten, claims, headRef}, communication. activity.instruction and activity.command hold prompt and command text: never read them, read only pid, sessionId, status, activity.phase, updatedAt.
pid_index.liveness: Rewritten every 5 s (ACTIVE_AGENT_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS) and on every status emit, deleted on clean exit. The vendor treats a record as stale when its pid is dead or updatedAt is older than 15 s (ACTIVE_AGENT_STALE_MS); a crash leaves the file until the next reader prunes it. Apply the same test.
pid_index.cli: `autohand agents` (interactive watcher) and `autohand agents --once` (one snapshot) print these records; `/agents` inside a session does the same. Official name for the feature: global Autohand session heartbeats.

working_signals.name: ~/.autohand/active-agents/<sessionId>.json: activity.phase != "idle" AND pid alive AND updatedAt within 15 s (status == "working" is a weaker second reading)
working_signals.meaning: Exact per-process turn state, and the pid field is the CLI's own process.pid, so no argv or cwd guessing. READ activity.phase, NOT status. Verification found that activity is rebuilt on every write from live isInstructionActive (getActivity -> buildActivity -> derivePhase in src/core/agent.ts and src/session/peers/PeerActivityPublisher.ts), while the top-level status is the value passed to the LAST update(): the 5 s timer calls update() with no argument, so it re-sends the cached status (ActiveAgentHeartbeat.update(status = this.status) in src/session/ActiveAgentRegistry.ts). status is only refreshed by emitStatus(), which runs on context-usage and provider events, and InstructionRunner.ts does not call it after clearing isInstructionActive, so status can lag the end of a turn by up to the next emitStatus. Source read only, never seen live. phase: idle (no turn), thinking (turn active, no tool), editing (write_file, apply_patch, replace_in_file, search_replace and the other editing tools), running_command (run_command or shell), waiting_input. Caveat: a permission prompt or question keeps the turn active, so phase becomes waiting_input, not idle: treat waiting_input as waiting, see waiting_signals. Source only: the probe cannot read a JSON field and has no per_session path for this file, so it cannot fire this signal; a reader needs a JSON-field signal. The mtime of this file alone proves nothing (rewritten every 5 s while idle).

The run_command tool runs `spawn(command, [], {shell: true})` (src/core/actionExecutor.ts, src/actions/command.ts), so a shell tool call is a DIRECT child `/bin/sh -c <command>` of the CLI process. Shell child means a shell tool call is running. Caveats, all inferred from source: (1) macOS /bin/sh may exec a single simple command in place, then the direct child carries the command's own name (case 9 in the README); (2) a shell child of an idle session appears when a `background` command outlives its turn; (3) hook commands also run through `spawn(..., {shell: true, detached})` (HookManager.ts), so a configured hook shows a short-lived shell child at pre-tool, stop and other events; (4) blind while the model streams or a non-shell tool (read_file, search, MCP) runs. Never count `caffeinate`, `osascript` (focus check before a desktop notification, src/utils/notification.ts), `afplay` (the sound-alert hook), `terminal-notifier` or `ahtraces`. `autohand --mode teammate` children are the same executable as their parent: ignore them, they are their own sessions.

Raise-only. conversation.jsonl gets one appended line per committed message (user prompt, assistant reply, tool result), and metadata.json is rewritten with a fresh lastActiveAt on each. A long model call or a long tool call writes nothing, so a stale mtime never proves idle. Needs the session id from the active-agents record (pid_index), because argv has none, so the probe's per_session lookup finds nothing for a plain launch. Window is a guess, unmeasured.

Weak fallback, unmeasured guess. The Ink TUI redraws a braille spinner while a turn runs, so some CPU is expected, but a turn waiting on the network burns almost none, and MCP servers started by the session sit in the same tree. Not verified: nothing was run.

waiting_signals.meaning: Exact and needs no setup. derivePhase() returns waiting_input while a turn is active AND peerAwaitingInputCount > 0, which beginAwaitingInput() raises around confirmDangerousAction (a tool permission or dangerous-action prompt) and executeAskFollowupQuestion (the ask_followup_question tool). status remains 'working' during the wait. Refreshed at most every 5 s after the state changes, so expect a lag of up to 5 s. Source only (src/session/peers/PeerActivityPublisher.ts, src/core/agent.ts).

Fires before the permission dialog is shown (context: tool, path, permission type). A hook can also answer it (exit 2 blocks; stdout JSON decision allow|deny|ask|block). Needs a hook installed. `permission-denied` fires when the user refuses.

HOOK_NOTIFICATION_TYPE is the NotificationOptions.reason from src/utils/notification.ts: confirmation (permission wait), question (ask_followup_question wait), task_complete (turn finished). Needs a hook installed. The desktop notification itself is skipped while the terminal is focused, but the hook still runs (listener is on the notification service; inferred, the focus gate was not traced).

OSC 0 window or tab title, written by src/ui/terminalTitle.ts to any real TTY (not with --json, --acp, --mode rpc): a braille spinner (⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏) while a turn runs, ◐ while it waits on the human, ✓ idle or done, ✗ failed; format `<marker> <session name> · Autohand`, or `<marker> Autohand Code` when the session has no name. In iTerm2 the tab is also coloured green, orange or red. A terminal host (cmux, kitty, iTerm2, Ghostty) can read it. It is the only signal that needs neither a file read nor a hook, and the only one that separates working from waiting for the person watching the tab. Source only.

hooks.config: hooks key in ~/.autohand/config.json (also config.toml, config.yaml, config.yml), <project>/.autohand/config.json (shareable; project hooks and MCP only apply after the workspace is trusted, stored in ~/.autohand/trusted-workspaces.json), <project>/.autohand/settings.local.json (personal), or a file named by --config. Two shapes: {"hooks":{"enabled":true,"hooks":[{"event":"stop","command":"...","description":"...","timeout":5000,"async":false,"matcher":"regex","filter":{"tool":[],"path":[]}}]}} and an event-keyed form. Commands run with `shell: true`; the event arrives as JSON on stdin and as HOOK_EVENT, HOOK_SESSION_ID, HOOK_WORKSPACE, HOOK_TOOL, HOOK_TURN_DURATION and about 70 more HOOK_* variables. Exit 2 blocks pre-tool and permission-request; stdout JSON {decision, reason, additionalContext} controls the flow. Manage with /hooks, /hooks list, /hooks manage; generated scripts land in ~/.autohand/hooks/generated/. Also: runtime extension hooks (api.hooks.on), JSON-RPC autohand.hook.* notifications in rpc and ACP mode, and an importer for other agents' hooks. `--bare` skips hooks entirely.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry: a case-insensitive search of src, docs, package.json, config.example.json, schema, scripts and README for opentelemetry, otlp and OTEL_ found nothing (the only hit is an optional vitest peer dependency in bun.lock). Autohand has its own, separate paths (docs/telemetry.md): product telemetry is OFF by default (telemetry.enabled, POST /v1/telemetry, queue ~/.autohand/telemetry/queue.json), cloud session sync is a second opt-in (telemetry.enableSessionSync), a version check runs on ordinary start-up (AUTOHAND_SKIP_PING=1 stops it), automatic error reports are ON unless autoReport.enabled is false, and the `ahtraces` companion (off until consent) syncs agent traces to console.autohand.ai. None of these is a local status feed.

notes: Not installed on this Mac: nothing was run and no session file was seen, so this is source and docs only. Best signal is the per-process heartbeat ~/.autohand/active-agents/<sessionId>.json (pid, status, activity.phase, 5 s cadence, 15 s stale): it gives an exact turn state, an exact waiting state (phase waiting_input while status stays working) and the pid-to-session map that argv cannot give. The current probe cannot read a JSON field, so until it can, the shell child of a tool call, the terminal title marker and CPU are what it has. There is no sleep assertion and no per-turn caffeinate; a caffeinate -dims -w <pid> child only appears after /go pairing and is held for the whole pairing, so do not count it. Two traps in matching: the CLI retitles itself to 'Autohand Code' (with a space) so flags vanish from ps, and bare `agent` is claimed by Autohand's installers, Grok Build and Cursor at once, so it is not matched. The ahtraces sidecar and Autohand Computer Use.app are helpers, not sessions. Verifier additions 2026-09-30: (1) read activity.phase, not the top-level status, for turn state; status is a cached value re-sent by the 5 s timer. (2) The VS Code extension bundles the CLI, so its child may not match any surface here. (3) Known matching limits, kept because no better discriminator exists: the node surface's args_contain '/bin/autohand' is a substring, so `node /any/bin/autohand/x.js` from a user's own project would read as a session; exclude_args is an exact match on any argument, so a prompt that is exactly `init`, `update`, `config` and so on hides a real session (README section 3 case 16). (4) The compiled-binary retitle is unknown, so a title-less `autohand` argv[0] still matches surface 3. The row is source-and-docs only and stays 'documented'.
